answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to place a stake in a public escrow contract, then earn reputation only through completed jobs that counterparties sign and that pass random audits. The signal is costly skin in the game: a Sybil operator must lock real capital for each persona and risks losing it when a fraud proof succeeds. A prism of independent reviewers can expose colluding ratings; timber-like durability comes from keeping the stake and verified history bound to the same key, so identities cannot cheaply reset after abuse.
